leading_positions.synthesis: Four of the eight round-1 configurations include B029, all with the same two laureates (Hidetoshi Katori, Jun Ye). Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce propose it as the whole prize; Danielsson proposes it as one of two parts, paired with B037. Shared ground: the magic-wavelength lattice scheme, the 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, cross-laboratory reproduction and a two-name credit. Not shared: citation wording (Kroll wants the measurement achievement, not only the idea; Lindroth and Pearce want it limited to the lattice scheme so that comb and ion-clock work is not re-awarded), how much weight the pending redefinition of the second carries, and whether the 2005 and 2012 prizes make the topic less new. Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson list B029 only as an alternative or fallback, not as their preferred configuration.

Two configurations name B031 as the whole prize, with the same trio (Allan H. MacDonald, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Rafi Bistritzer) and near-identical citations covering the prediction of flat moire bands at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states. They share the prediction-then-experiment argument and fast reproduction by many groups. Both also name the weaknesses themselves: unresolved pairing mechanism, device-to-device variability, a field under ten years old, and the omission of Cao and other experimentalists. Mehlig names B029 as an alternative and as the cleaner fallback if the B031 credit set is judged unsound; Eriksson names B016 and B029.

Danielsson's is the only two-part configuration: the B029 clocks pair plus a single-laureate B037 (Francis Halzen) for high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and IceCube. He presents it as two distinct achievements within a three-name limit and names B012 and B016 as fallbacks if B037 fails on attribution. No other member's configuration includes B037. Danielsson's own case against it is the sole credit for a large collaboration and the unknown origin of most of the flux.

Johansson alone prefers circuit quantum electrodynamics, crediting Alexandre Blais, Robert J. Schoelkopf and Andreas Wallraff. His own statement raises three problems: adjacency to the 2025 prize on superconducting-circuit tunnelling, four credited names for three places (he drops Girvin), and his closeness to the field. His alternatives are B029 and B018. Kroll and Lindroth, who prefer B029, also raise adjacency and the four-to-three problem in their statements.

Olsson alone prefers nitrogen-vacancy centres, with a two-name credit (Jorg Wrachtrup, Fedor Jelezko) that omits Mikhail Lukin, who is on the ballot. She states that this candidate has the least support among colleagues and that her first place is not evidence of wider support. Her alternatives are B031 and B029. She argues that NV sensing already has a concrete adoption record; others in the files question the discovery boundary and the credit against Hanson, Awschalom and other groups.

areas_of_agreement: B029 appears in four of the eight explicit configurations and is also named as an alternative by each of the four members who do not prefer it (Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson), so it is the one ballot that is both preferred and accepted as a serious candidate across several different leanings. Its two-name credit (Katori, Ye) is described as the cleanest on the shortlist by members who prefer other candidates.

Members who do not prefer B031 (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce) describe the flat-band prediction and correlated phases as a serious and widely reproduced result in their statements, or list it as an alternative, and place their reservations on maturity and credit.

Members across positions agree that the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits is relevant to how B004 is read, although they differ on whether it counts against the candidate (Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth address it directly).
Several members state that the weaknesses of their own preferred candidate are real: attribution for B031, B001 and B037, and novelty relative to earlier prizes for B029.
No statement disputes that the physics of the preferred candidates is real; the disagreements are about credit, timing, and whether a measurement advance is a discovery.
scientific_disputes: Measurement advance versus new behaviour of matter: Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce value a clean, reproduced 10^-18 metric; Eriksson and Mehlig value a new regime of correlated matter that followed a theoretical prediction; Eriksson calls B029 a refinement of precision spectroscopy more than a new behaviour.

Novelty of B029 relative to the 2005 prize (frequency comb) and the 2012 prize (single-ion control): Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce say neither covered a many-atom magic-wavelength lattice at 10^-18; Olsson and Eriksson say the territory has largely been honoured; Mehlig calls the clock a refinement of the ruler that those prizes created.

Whether the single-particle flat-band picture in B031 is the durable result that can be recognised now, or whether the unresolved many-body ground state and pairing mechanism make recognition premature (Eriksson and Mehlig versus Danielsson, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce, with Lindroth and Pearce deferring to condensed-matter colleagues).

Whether B004 is a distinct discovery (coherent single-excitation exchange between a circuit and a photon) or too close to the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits; Johansson argues the former, Kroll and Lindroth stress the latter as an obstacle.

Whether the NV-centre case (B001) rests on original single-spin detection and control, or on a broader quantum-sensing field whose record is still being established (Olsson versus Kroll, Pearce and Johansson).

Whether the prospective payoffs of clocks (redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy, constants and dark-matter searches) belong in the case; Danielsson asks that the citation rest on demonstrated performance, while Olsson's concern is that the benefit is still modest.
attribution_disputes: B029: whether Katori (magic-wavelength proposal, 2001-2003) and Ye (10^-18 systematics, many-body clock) are the right pair, given Lemonde, Peik and Hollberg on the proposal side and Ludlow, Bloom, Hinkley, Lemke, Kitagawa and the ion-clock groups on the achievement side. Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce all raise this; none proposes a different pair.

B031: Bistritzer as third laureate versus a two-name prediction-plus-experiment pair (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero), which Eriksson and Mehlig name in their responses to Olsson; Yuan Cao, Fatemi and Dean's group are not credited, and earlier continuum-model theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) bears on how the prediction is worded.

B004: four credited names for three places. Johansson drops Girvin and keeps Blais; the statements of Kroll and Lindroth say the record does not settle this, and Koch, Houck and others on the transmon and amplifier work lie outside the credited set.
B037: a single laureate (Halzen) for an observatory collaboration with an AMANDA precursor and earlier deep-water and deep-ice pioneers (Danielsson).

B001: Wrachtrup and Jelezko only (Olsson) versus a quantum-sensing framing that would bring in Lukin; Hanson and Awschalom are outside the credited set, and Wrachtrup appears in overlapping candidates.

The configurations listed as alternatives carry unresolved credit too: B013 (the late Jan van Paradijs and the optical-identification groups are not credited), B012 (three collaboration leaders out of thousands, with the 2013 prize already given for the discovery), and B016 (Zhang's death, the two- versus three-dimensional split, and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang).
maturity_disputes: B031: the field is under ten years old, the pairing mechanism is unresolved and twist-angle disorder limits device-to-device reproducibility; Eriksson and Mehlig regard the phenomenon as established enough, while Danielsson, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce raise timing as a reservation and Lindroth defers to condensed-matter colleagues.

B029: the formal redefinition of the second has not happened; Kroll asks whether to wait for it, whereas Lindroth and Pearce regard cross-laboratory comparisons at 10^-18 as already sufficient for recognition.

B037: the diffuse flux is established, but the TXS 0506+056 association is about 3 sigma, the Galactic-plane result is recent and the origin of most of the flux is unknown; Danielsson judges the discovery of the flux to be the matured result, Pearce's own statement notes the maturity question.
B004: Johansson treats timing as a question of sequence, not of merit; Lindroth explicitly asks the committee to decide whether a second consecutive superconducting-circuit prize is defensible.
B001: Olsson points to broad adoption already; Kroll and Johansson say the biological sensing claims are still developing.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: Director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and a Chalmers theorist in superconducting circuits, with acquaintance with circuit-QED principals; he flags a possible recusal issue for B004 and defers to the chair on whether to step back from that candidate. Chalmers colleagues (Delsing, Wilson, Kockum) work on related waveguide QED, and Chalmers hosted 2025 laureates as WACQT guest researchers.

Kroll: spent a year of his PhD in John Hall's laboratory (Hall is a 2005 laureate, not a credited name in B029); notes closeness to the laser-spectroscopy community; his work on rare-earth crystals and quantum memories is adjacent to B001 and B004, and his WACQT role overlaps institutionally with Chalmers, relevant if B004 is discussed.

Lindroth: long-time close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and co-author with the Lund attosecond group and Ursula Keller's group; none is a credited name, and she says her subfield (precision atomic physics) may bias her toward B029, B044 and B018.

Pearce (chair): no tie to Katori, Ye or their groups for B029; his own work in gamma-ray astronomy and polarimetry (Fermi-LAT, PAMELA, XL-Calibur) is adjacent to B013, his alternative, and to B037, which appears in Danielsson's configuration, so he would weigh recusal on those if they became decisive. He is also one of the four supporters of B029 and has relied on colleagues for condensed-matter judgements.

Mehlig: no specific conflict; notes that he shares the Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson, whose fields touch B004 and B001. Olsson notes that she shares Chalmers with Johansson.
Danielsson and Eriksson: no specific conflict stated for any shortlisted candidate.
questions_for_round2: Johansson has flagged B004 as a possible recusal and deferred to the chair: should he step back from B004 discussion and any ballot on it, and does Kroll's WACQT overlap require any similar handling?

For B029, is crediting only Katori and Ye adequate given the proposal history (Lemonde, Peik, Hollberg) and the team work at JILA, PTB, RIKEN, NIST and SYRTE, and can a citation be worded around the magic-wavelength lattice clock at 10^-18 without implicitly re-awarding the comb (2005) and ion-control (2012) prizes?

Do Lindroth and Kroll, as the atomic physicists, confirm that the proposal-history and ion-clock credit questions on B029 do not change the two-name set, and should the committee request an outside assessment before ranking it?
Is the committee willing to recognise B029 before the formal redefinition of the second, or does it want that outcome treated as a condition?

For B031, should the theory credit be Bistritzer and MacDonald together, or should the committee consider a two-name prediction-plus-experiment pair, and how will it explain the omission of Cao, Fatemi and Dean's group?

Can Eriksson and Mehlig say how many independent groups have reproduced superconductivity at the magic angle, and whether the unresolved pairing mechanism is a reason to defer or only a footnote to the discovery?

If a two-part configuration is considered, does the committee see any scientific kinship between B029 and B037, and can Halzen as sole credit for B037 be defended, or would that part need a different credited set?

On B004, are Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth prepared to say whether the 2025 prize is a decisive obstacle or merely a sequencing consideration, and which of Blais and Girvin belongs in the third place?
What would members who currently prefer B031, B004, B001 or B037 need to see to move their first choice to another ballot, and which fallback does each accept?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit round-1 configurations, B029 is in four of eight (as the whole prize for three members and one part of two for Danielsson), B031 is the whole prize for two, and B004, B001 and the B037 part each have one supporter. This count covers stated configurations only, and the chair is one of the four B029 supporters. The B029 and B031 cases differ mainly in kind (a clean, reproduced measurement advance with novelty questions, versus a newer discovery with a contested credit set and an open mechanism) and not in whether the physics is real. The decisive questions for round 2 look to be the credit wording and set for B029 and B031, the recusal question on B004, and whether a second prize part is wanted.
